title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
spaceBreakdown:
- int j, n: two integers → O(1)
- s.substr(0, j): returned output, not counted
- not counted: input string s (passed by value, modified in place)
approach: Use two pointers on the input string itself: a read pointer `i` scans left to right, and a write pointer `j` marks the current end of the result being built in place. For each character `s[i]`, if it matches the character just before the write position (`s[j-1]`), decrement `j` to undo the last write; otherwise, write `s[i]` at position `j` and advance `j`. This naturally handles cascading removals because after a pop, the next comparison uses the new top. Return `s.substr(0, j)`.
hints: When two adjacent equal letters are removed, what happens to the letters that were on either side of that pair? The string length can be up to 10^5.

Use two pointers on the string itself: a read pointer scans forward, and a write pointer marks the "top" of the result. On "abbaca": read 'a'→write (j=1); read 'b'→write (j=2); read 'b'→matches s[j-1], pop (j=1); read 'a'→matches s[j-1], pop (j=0); read 'c'→write (j=1); read 'a'→write (j=2). Return s[0..1]="ca".

**Single character** - n=1, no adjacent pair exists.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: "a"`
⚠️ Bug: returning s.substr(0, j-1) instead of s.substr(0, j) → returns ""

**Wrong index** - comparing the wrong position causes incorrect pops.
`Input: s = "azxxzy"` → `Expected: "ay"`
⚠️ Bug: comparing s[j] instead of s[j-1] with s[i] → returns ""

**No cascading re-check** - a removal exposes a new pair that must also be removed.
`Input: s = "abbaca"` → `Expected: "ca"`
⚠️ Bug: a single pass that skips both characters of a matched pair without re-checking the boundary → returns "aaca"

**All equal, even length** - every character cancels.
`Input: s = "aaaa"` → `Expected: ""`
⚠️ Bug: returning s instead of s.substr(0, j) → returns "aaaa"

followUps.q: Instead of removing pairs, remove exactly k adjacent equal letters. How does the approach change?
followUps.a: Track a run-length count at the write position instead of comparing single characters. When the run reaches k, roll the write pointer back by k and resume comparing against the new top. Time stays O(n), space stays O(1).

followUps.q: The input arrives as a stream of unknown length. How do you adapt?
followUps.a: Keep a buffer (acting as the write pointer's contents) and apply the same push/pop logic per character. Space becomes O(n) in the worst case (no duplicates), since you cannot modify a stream in place.

followUps.q: What if after removing all adjacent duplicates, you must also reverse the result?
followUps.a: Run the two-pointer deduplication, then reverse s[0..j-1] in place. Time stays O(n), space stays O(1).
